claim: Microglia and macrophages are present in brain tumors.
source: It is now clear that microglia and macrophages are present in brain tumors, but whether or how they affect initiation and development of tumors is not known.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Macrophages and microglia respond immediately upon oncogene activation in the brain.
source: Exploiting the advantages of the zebrafish (Danio rerio) model, we showed that macrophages and microglia respond immediately upon oncogene activation in the brain.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Overexpression of human AKT1 within neural cells of larval zebrafish led to a significant increase in the macrophage and microglia populations.
source: Overexpression of human AKT1 within neural cells of larval zebrafish led to a significant increase in the macrophage and microglia populations.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative data in Figure 2B.

claim: The increase in macrophage and microglia populations was caused by the infiltration of peripheral macrophages into the brain mediated via Sdf1b-Cxcr4b signaling.
source: By using a combination of transgenic and mutant zebrafish lines, we showed that this increase was caused by the infiltration of peripheral macrophages into the brain mediated via Sdf1b-Cxcr4b signaling.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 4, 5, 6, and 7.

claim: Confocal live imaging reveals highly dynamic interactions between macrophages/microglia and pre-neoplastic cells, which do not result in phagocytosis of pre-neoplastic cells.
source: Intriguingly, confocal live imaging reveals highly dynamic interactions between macrophages/microglia and pre-neoplastic cells, which do not result in phagocytosis of pre-neoplastic cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by live imaging data in Figure 3 and Videos 1-4.

claim: Depletion of macrophages and microglia resulted in a significant reduction of oncogenic cell proliferation.
source: Finally, depletion of macrophages and microglia resulted in a significant reduction of oncogenic cell proliferation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 8.

claim: Macrophages and microglia show tumor promoting functions already during the earliest stages of the developing tumor microenvironment.
source: Thus, macrophages and microglia show tumor promoting functions already during the earliest stages of the developing tumor microenvironment.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Microglia are the resident macrophages of the brain.
source: Microglia are the resident macrophages of the brain (for review see [Kettenmann et al., 2011; Casano and Peri, 2015]).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Microglia are derived from primitive macrophages that invade the brain during development.
source: Microglia are derived from primitive macrophages that invade the brain during development (Ginhoux et al., 2010; Schulz et al., 2012; Herbomel et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Microglia and infiltrating macrophages have been shown to infiltrate high-grade gliomas and can account for up to 30% of the tumoral mass.
source: Microglia and infiltrating macrophages have been shown to infiltrate high-grade gliomas and can account for up to 30% of the tumoral mass (Graeber et al., 2002; Badie and Schartner, 2001; Li and Graeber, 2012; Yang et al., 2010; Coniglio and Segall, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Macrophages and microglia display pro-tumoural functions and promote tumor growth.
source: Instead of anti-tumoural activity, they display pro-tumoural functions and promote tumor growth.
evidence: This is established knowledge stated in the introduction.

claim: Macrophages and microglia have been shown to promote tumor cell proliferation and invasiveness, to modify the extracellular matrix, to induce angiogenesis and to induce an immunosuppressive environment promoting tumor growth.
source: Macrophages and microglia have been shown to promote tumor cell proliferation and invasiveness, to modify the extracellular matrix, to induce angiogenesis and to induce an immunosuppressive environment promoting tumor growth (Zhai et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2012; Markovic et al., 2005; Komohara et al., 2008; Pyonteck et al., 2013; Wu et al., 2010; Hambardzumyan et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2013; Ellert-Miklaszewska et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Pro-tumoural functions of macrophages and microglia seem to be independent of the tumor grade, as they have also been described for low-grade gliomas.
source: Interestingly, these pro-tumoural functions seem to be independent of the tumor grade, as they have also been described for low-grade gliomas (Daginakatte and Gutmann, 2007; Daginakatte et al., 2008; Simmons et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The earliest responses of macrophages and microglia to cancerous cells in the brain have not been addressed so far.
source: However, the earliest responses of macrophages and microglia to cancerous cells in the brain have not been addressed so far.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that the study addresses.

claim: The zebrafish is a powerful tool to study microglia.
source: We and others have already demonstrated that the zebrafish is a powerful tool to study microglia (Peri and Nüsslein-Volhard, 2008; Sieger et al., 2012; Xu et al., 2016; Oosterhof et al., 2017; Svahn et al., 2013; Shiau et al., 2013; Shen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The small size of the zebrafish brain allows imaging of the entire microglial network and its responses to pathological events.
source: Besides the genetic and optical advantages of the zebrafish larvae, the small size of the zebrafish brain allows imaging of the entire microglial network and its responses to pathological events.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the zebrafish model based on established knowledge.

claim: Recent work has highlighted the suitability of the larval zebrafish model to investigate brain tumor growth.
source: Furthermore, recent work has highlighted the suitability of the larval zebrafish model to investigate brain tumor growth (Ju et al., 2014; Mayrhofer et al., 2017; Shin et al., 2012; Ju et al., 2015; Lal et al., 2012; Kitambi et al., 2014; Geiger et al., 2008; Lally et al., 2007); Yang et al., 2013; Jung et al., 2013; Hamilton et al. (2016); Eden et al., 2015; Welker et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: AKT1 is a downstream serine-threonine kinase in the RTK/PTEN/PI3K pathway which is highly activated in the majority of human glioblastomas.
source: AKT1 is a downstream serine-threonine kinase in the RTK/PTEN/PI3K pathway which is highly activated in the majority of human glioblastomas (McLendon and Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Human AKT1 has been reported previously to induce malignant transformations in various neural cell types in zebrafish leading to glioma growth.
source: Human AKT1 has been reported previously to induce malignant transformations in various neural cell types in zebrafish leading to glioma growth (Mayrhofer et al., 2017; Jung et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Expression of AKT1 led to morphological transformations resulting in larger cells with an abnormal morphology.
source: During the course of development, AKT1 expression-induced morphological transformations resulting in larger cells with an abnormal morphology which was not observed upon injection of a lexOP:tagRFP control construct (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Immunohistochemistry using an anti-AKT1 antibody revealed strong expression of the human AKT1 protein upon lexOP:AKT1-lexOP:tagRFP construct injection.
source: Immunohistochemistry using an anti-AKT1 antibody revealed strong expression of the human AKT1 protein upon lexOP:AKT1-lexOP:tagRFP construct injection (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Expression of AKT1 led to an early onset of expression of Synaptophysin.
source: Indeed, expression of AKT1 led to an early onset of expression of Synaptophysin, which was not observed in controls (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Synaptophysin has been shown to be expressed in CNS tumors with neuronal differentiation as well as in neuroendocrine tumors.
source: To test for differentiation in AKT1 overexpressing cells, we performed immunohistochemistry for the differentiation marker Synaptophysin, which has been shown to be expressed in CNS tumors with neuronal differentiation as well as in neuroendocrine tumors (Wiedenmann et al., 1986).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: GFAP was neither detected in AKT1-expressing cells nor in RFP control cells at 8 dpf.
source: GFAP was neither detected in AKT1-expressing cells nor in RFP control cells at 8 dpf (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Oncogenic alterations have been previously shown to induce dedifferentiation of neuronal cells.
source: Intriguingly, oncogenic alterations have been previously shown to induce dedifferentiation of neuronal cells (Friedmann-Morvinski et al., 2012), thus we wondered if AKT1 overexpression is capable of inducing dedifferentiation in zebrafish neural cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Immunohistochemistry for the stem cell marker Sox2 revealed a subset of AKT1 cells which were positive for Sox2 while none of the RFP control cells appeared to be positive for Sox2.
source: Interestingly, immunohistochemistry for the stem cell marker Sox2 revealed a subset of AKT1 cells which were positive for Sox2 while none of the RFP control cells appeared to be positive for Sox2 (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The number of proliferating AKT1-positive cells was significantly increased compared to control RFP cells.
source: Furthermore, the number of proliferating AKT1-positive cells was significantly increased compared to control RFP cells (assessed by immunostaining for proliferating cell nuclear antigen (PCNA); Figure 1G).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The oncogene expression led to significant impairment in survival with only 35.6% (62/174 larvae) surviving until 30 days post-fertilization (dpf) upon AKT1 overexpression compared to 90.8% (118/130 larvae) in controls.
source: Finally, the oncogene expression led to significant impairment in survival with only 35.6% (62/174 larvae) surviving until 30 days post-fertilization (dpf) upon AKT1 overexpression compared to 90.8% (118/130 larvae) in controls (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by survival data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Examination of 20 AKT1 expressing fish at 1 month of age showed persistent expression of the RFP-tag in the brain, with variable mosaicism.
source: Examination of 20 AKT1 expressing fish at 1 month of age showed persistent expression of the RFP-tag in the brain, with variable mosaicism (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–H).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–H.

claim: Some of the RFP expressing cells showed neuronal features, including RFP-labeled axons and dendrites.
source: Some of the RFP expressing cells showed neuronal features, including RFP-labeled axons and dendrites (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), while 1/3 of the brains showed large clones of RFP-expressing cells, which grew deeply in the brain parenchyma, apparently without disrupting the brain architecture.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Immunostaining of these areas with a panel of antisera (PCNA, AKT1, GFAP and Synaptophysin) showed disrupted cell architecture, with increased mitotic figures, as well as positive staining for AKT1, GFAP and Synaptophysin, suggesting abnormal growth and differentiation, suggestive of brain tumors with mixed neuronal and glial components.
source: Immunostaining of these areas with a panel of antisera (PCNA, AKT1, GFAP and Synaptophysin) showed disrupted cell architecture, with increased mitotic figures, as well as positive staining for AKT1, GFAP and Synaptophysin, suggesting abnormal growth and differentiation, suggestive of brain tumors with mixed neuronal and glial components (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I–N).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1I–N.

claim: The heterogeneous population of cells detected within these tumors is most probably a result of the early dedifferentiation events that we observed.
source: The heterogeneous population of cells detected within these tumors is most probably a result of the early dedifferentiation events that we observed (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is an inference based on the dedifferentiation data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: This is in line with previous observations in rodent models, showing that dedifferentiated cells are capable of generating a NSC or progenitor state which gives rise to heterogeneous populations observed in mature tumors.
source: This is in line with previous observations in rodent models, showing that dedifferentiated cells are capable of generating a NSC or progenitor state which gives rise to heterogeneous populations observed in mature tumors (Friedmann-Morvinski et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison to established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: There was a significant increase in microglia numbers in AKT1-positive brains when compared to controls at 8 dpf.
source: Interestingly, at this early time point we observed a significant increase in microglia numbers in AKT1-positive brains when compared to controls (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Under normal physiological conditions, microglia show a highly ramified phenotype with several fine processes that are constantly extended and retracted to survey their environment.
source: Under normal physiological conditions, microglia show a highly ramified phenotype with several fine processes that are constantly extended and retracted to survey their environment (Nimmerjahn et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: In response to a pathological insult in the brain, the microglia retract their processes and assume an amoeboid morphology which reflects their activation.
source: In response to a pathological insult in the brain, the microglia retract their processes and assume an amoeboid morphology which reflects their activation (Karperien et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: This change in morphology leads to a change in the ratio of the microglia cell surface to microglia cell volume, which can be used as a read out for their activation.
source: This change in morphology leads to a change in the ratio of the microglia cell surface to microglia cell volume, which can be used as a read out for their activation (Gyoneva et al., 2014) (Figure 2Ai–iii).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: There was a significantly higher percentage of amoeboid (activated) microglia in AKT1 overexpressing brains compared to control brains at 8 dpf.
source: This analysis showed a significantly higher percentage of amoeboid (activated) microglia in AKT1 overexpressing brains compared to control brains (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: In control embryos, microglia showed the typical ramified morphology, and cell surface contacts between microglia and control RFP cells were only occasionally observed and of short durations.
source: In control embryos, microglia showed the typical ramified morphology, and cell surface contacts between microglia and control RFP cells were only occasionally observed and of short durations (Figure 3A, Video 1, n = 7 samples analyzed).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3A and Video 1.

claim: The density of microglia within AKT1-expressing brains was high and most microglial cells showed an amoeboid morphology.
source: In line with our previous observations based on 4C4 immunohistochemistry (Figure 2), the density of microglia within AKT1-expressing brains was high and most microglial cells showed an amoeboid morphology (Figure 3B, Video 2, n = 9 samples analyzed).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Video 2.

claim: Microglia were observed to stay within close vicinity to AKT1 positive cells throughout the duration of the experiment and most microglial cells were in direct surface contact with the oncogenic cells.
source: Interestingly, microglia were observed to stay within close vicinity to AKT1 positive cells throughout the duration of the experiment and most microglial cells were in direct surface contact with the oncogenic cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Video 2.

claim: Microglia were observed to flatten their surfaces against the surfaces of AKT1-positive cells and then moving their surfaces around the surfaces of AKT1 cells for hours.
source: Microglia were observed to flatten their surfaces against the surfaces of AKT1-positive cells and then moving their surfaces around the surfaces of AKT1 cells for hours (Figure 3B, arrowheads, Video 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Video 2.

claim: Other microglial cells showed interactions with several AKT1-positive cells by constantly expanding and retracting their processes upon contact with surfaces of AKT1 positive cells.
source: Other microglial cells showed interactions with several AKT1-positive cells by constantly expanding and retracting their processes upon contact with surfaces of AKT1 positive cells (Figure 3B, arrows, Video 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3B and Video 2.

claim: Many of these interactions were observed for several hours without any disruption.
source: Importantly, many of these interactions were observed for several hours without any disruption.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging data.

claim: Based on the persistence of these interactions it is unlikely that these were random contacts simply enforced by the high density of microglial and AKT1-positive cells.
source: Thus, based on the persistence of these interactions it is unlikely that these were random contacts simply enforced by the high density of microglial and AKT1-positive cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the live imaging data.

claim: In larvae with lower numbers and isolated AKT1-positive cells, microglia were frequently seen to interact with AKT1-positive cells.
source: In these larvae, microglia were frequently seen to interact with AKT1-positive cells (Figure 3C,D Video 3 and 4, n = 6 samples analyzed).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 3C,D and Videos 3 and 4.

claim: Microglia are pro-actively interacting with AKT1-positive cells.
source: Thus, microglia are pro-actively interacting with AKT1-positive cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the live imaging data showing targeted interactions.

claim: The observed interactions were not 'anti-tumoral' as we did not observe phagocytosis of AKT1-expressing cells.
source: Importantly, the observed interactions were not 'anti-tumoral' as we did not observe phagocytosis of AKT1-expressing cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on the absence of phagocytosis in live imaging data.

claim: We did not detect a difference in the number of PCNA positive microglia when comparing AKT1-positive brains to control brains.
source: Interestingly, we did not detect a difference in the number of PCNA positive microglia when comparing AKT1-positive brains to control brains (not shown).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on immunostaining data.

claim: The presence of pre-neoplastic cells in the brain might cause an infiltration of peripheral macrophages, which then differentiate into 4C4-positive microglia-like cells.
source: Thus, we speculated that the presence of pre-neoplastic cells in the brain might cause an infiltration of peripheral macrophages, which then differentiate into 4C4-positive microglia-like cells.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the absence of microglial proliferation.

claim: Significantly higher numbers of L-plastin+/4C4- cells were detected within the brain parenchyma upon AKT1 overexpression at 8 dpf.
source: Indeed, we detected significantly higher numbers of L-plastin+/4C4- cells within the brain parenchyma upon AKT1 overexpression at 8 dpf, which resemble either newly infiltrated macrophages or neutrophils (Figure 4A,Bi).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4A,Bi.

claim: AKT1 overexpression in transgenic mpx:GFP zebrafish showed no infiltration of neutrophils.
source: This experiment showed no infiltration of neutrophils upon AKT1 overexpression (data not shown), thus infiltrated L-plastin+/4C4- cells were solely macrophages.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on experimental data.

claim: There was a significant increase in the total amount of all L-plastin+ cells following the overexpression of AKT1 compared to age-matched controls.
source: In line with the previous results on increased microglial numbers, we detected a significant increase in the total amount of all L-plastin+ cells following the overexpression of AKT1 compared to age-matched controls (Figure 4A,Biii).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4A,Biii.

claim: Within the population of L-plastin+ cells, the majority of cells were positive for 4C4.
source: Within this population of L-plastin+ cells, the majority of cells were positive for 4C4 (Figure 4Bii).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4Bii.

claim: Infiltrated macrophages differentiated into microglia-like cells, leading to the higher numbers of 4C4-positive cells in AKT1-positive brains.
source: As we did not detect proliferation of resident microglia, we hypothesized that infiltrated macrophages differentiated into microglia-like cells, leading to the higher numbers of 4C4-positive cells in AKT1-positive brains.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the absence of microglial proliferation and the presence of infiltrating macrophages.

claim: At 3 dpf, there was a 4.5-fold increase in the number of L-plastin+/4C4- cells in AKT1 positive brains compared to controls.
source: Importantly, at 3 dpf we detected a 4.5-fold increase in the number of L-plastin+/4C4- cells in AKT1 positive brains compared to controls (Figure 4Ci).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4Ci.

claim: Numbers for 4C4-positive microglia were similar to controls at 3 dpf.
source: However, numbers for 4C4-positive microglia were similar to controls (Figure 4Cii).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4Cii.

claim: L-plastin+/4C4- cells at 3 dpf represented newly infiltrated macrophages.
source: Thus, these L-plastin+/4C4- cells represented newly infiltrated macrophages.
evidence: This is an inference based on the timing and marker expression.

claim: Infiltrated macrophages differentiated into microglia like (4C4+) cells over time.
source: As numbers of 4C4+ cells were only increased at later time points (Figure 4Bii) we conclude that these infiltrated macrophages differentiated into microglia like (4C4+) cells over time.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the temporal changes in cell populations.

claim: p2ry12-GFP-/mCherry+ macrophages were detected at the dorsal periphery of AKT1-positive brains at 5.5 dpf.
source: Intriguingly, we detected p2ry12-GFP-/mCherry+ macrophages at the dorsal periphery of AKT1-positive brains (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) at 5.5 dpf.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Some of these macrophages infiltrated the brain parenchyma and started expressing GFP over time, showing their differentiation toward a p2ry12-GFP+/mCherry+ microglia-like cell.
source: Eventually, some of these macrophages infiltrated the brain parenchyma and started expressing GFP over time, showing their differentiation toward a p2ry12-GFP+/mCherry+ microglia-like cell (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, arrowheads, Video 5).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Video 5.

claim: These infiltration and differentiation events were not observed in control larvae.
source: These infiltration and differentiation events were not observed in control larvae (not shown), which is in line with previously published data showing that developmental colonization of the brain by primitive macrophages is happening before 4.5 dpf (Casano et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by the absence of these events in controls and comparison to published data.

claim: Similar observations have been made recently in a rodent glioma model where infiltrating monocytes take on a microglia-like identity.
source: Importantly, similar observations have been made recently in a rodent glioma model where infiltrating monocytes take on a microglia-like identity (Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a comparison to established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The chemokine receptor Cxcr4's role in the recruitment of tumor supportive macrophages has been shown previously.
source: To address the underlying mechanism, we focused on the chemokine receptor Cxcr4 as its role in the recruitment of tumor supportive macrophages has been shown previously (Beider et al., 2014; Boimel et al., 2012; Hughes et al., 2015; Arnò et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Overexpression of AKT1 in the cxcr4b-/- mutant induces alterations as observed in wild-type larvae.
source: Thus, overexpression of AKT1 in the cxcr4b-/- mutant induces alterations as observed in wild-type larvae.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on immunostaining data shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: Overexpression of AKT1 in the cxcr4b-/- mutant did not lead to an increase in microglia numbers compared to overexpression of AKT1 in wild-type larvae.
source: However, overexpression of AKT1 in the cxcr4b-/- mutant did not lead to an increase in microglia numbers compared to overexpression of AKT1 in wild-type larvae (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Microglia numbers were similar in cxcr4b-/- controls and wild-type controls, showing that Cxcr4b signaling is not needed for the normal developmental population of the brain by microglia.
source: Notably, microglia numbers were similar in cxcr4b-/- controls and wild-type controls, showing that Cxcr4b signaling is not needed for the normal developmental population of the brain by microglia (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Cxcr4b signaling is either required for the infiltration of macrophages upon AKT1 overexpression or for their differentiation into 4C4-positive microglia-like cells.
source: Thus, Cxcr4b signaling is either required for the infiltration of macrophages upon AKT1 overexpression or for their differentiation into 4C4-positive microglia-like cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the absence of increased microglia numbers in the cxcr4b-/- mutant.

claim: The number of newly infiltrated macrophages (L-plastin+/4C4-) did not change upon AKT1 overexpression in the cxcr4b-/- mutant.
source: Intriguingly, the number of newly infiltrated macrophages (L-plastin+/4C4-) did not change upon AKT1 overexpression in the cxcr4b-/- mutant (Figure 5Ei).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5Ei.

claim: We did not detect an increase in the total number of all L-plastin+ cells upon AKT1 overexpression in the cxcr4b-/- mutant.
source: In line with this, we did not detect an increase in the total number of all L-plastin+ cells upon AKT1 overexpression in the cxcr4b-/- mutant (Figure 5Eii).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5Eii.

claim: cxcr4b-/- mutant zebrafish showed similar numbers of peripheral macrophages as wild-type zebrafish.
source: Importantly, cxcr4b-/- mutant zebrafish showed similar numbers of peripheral macrophages as wild-type zebrafish (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), thus the lack of infiltration of L-plastin+ cells was not due to a general deficiency in peripheral macrophages.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Macrophages in cxcr4b-/- mutant embryos showed normal recruitment and function during mycobacterial infections in a recent study.
source: Furthermore, macrophages in cxcr4b-/- mutant embryos showed normal recruitment and function during mycobacterial infections in a recent study (Torraca et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Cxcr4b signaling is specifically required for the infiltration of macrophages upon AKT1 overexpression in the brain.
source: Thus, Cxcr4b signaling is specifically required for the infiltration of macrophages upon AKT1 overexpression in the brain.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data showing lack of infiltration in the cxcr4b-/- mutant.

claim: There was an almost 50% reduced proliferation rate of AKT1-positive cells in the cxcr4b-/- mutant compared to the wild-type larvae following overexpression of AKT1.
source: Interestingly, while no observable impact on proliferating control-RFP cells was detected (Figure 5F), we detected an almost 50% reduced proliferation rate of AKT1-positive cells in the cxcr4b-/- mutant compared to the wild-type larvae following overexpression of AKT1 (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Cxcr4b signaling is required for the infiltration of macrophages and subsequent increase in 4C4-positive microglia numbers in AKT1 positive brains.
source: These results show that Cxcr4b signaling is required for the infiltration of macrophages and subsequent increase in 4C4-positive microglia numbers in AKT1 positive brains.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data from the cxcr4b-/- mutant experiments.

claim: These data imply an impact of macrophages and microglia on the proliferation rate of pre-neoplastic cells.
source: In addition, these data imply an impact of macrophages and microglia on the proliferation rate of pre-neoplastic cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the reduced proliferation in the cxcr4b-/- mutant.

claim: Cxcr4b might have a direct role in AKT1 positive cells and might be necessary for increased proliferation.
source: Alternatively, Cxcr4b might have a direct role in AKT1 positive cells and might be necessary for increased proliferation.
evidence: This is a speculation about an alternative explanation for the reduced proliferation.

claim: The rescue of Cxcr4b in macrophages/microglia led to an increase in 4C4 microglia numbers upon AKT1 overexpression in the cxcr4b-/- mutant.
source: Interestingly, the rescue of Cxcr4b in macrophages/microglia led to an increase in 4C4 microglia numbers upon AKT1 overexpression in the cxcr4b-/- mutant (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The specific rescue of Cxcr4b expression in AKT1 positive neural cells did not lead to increased microglia numbers.
source: On the contrary, the specific rescue of Cxcr4b expression in AKT1 positive neural cells did not lead to increased microglia numbers (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Cxcr4b function is needed cell autonomously in macrophages and microglia for an increase in microglial numbers induced by AKT1-overexpressing cells.
source: These results show that Cxcr4b function is needed cell autonomously in macrophages and microglia for an increase in microglial numbers induced by AKT1-overexpressing cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cell-specific rescue experiments.

claim: The Cxcr4b rescue in AKT1-positive neural cells did not increase their proliferation rates.
source: Interestingly, while the Cxcr4b rescue in AKT1-positive neural cells did not increase their proliferation rates (Figure 6D), the specific rescue of Cxcr4b expression in macrophages and microglia led to a 70% increase in proliferation rates of AKT1-positive cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The specific rescue of Cxcr4b expression in macrophages and microglia led to a 70% increase in proliferation rates of AKT1-positive cells.
source: Interestingly, while the Cxcr4b rescue in AKT1-positive neural cells did not increase their proliferation rates (Figure 6D), the specific rescue of Cxcr4b expression in macrophages and microglia led to a 70% increase in proliferation rates of AKT1-positive cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Cxcr4b signaling is not required in AKT1-positive neural cells to increase their proliferation rates.
source: Thus, Cxcr4b signaling is not required in AKT1-positive neural cells to increase their proliferation rates.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cell-specific rescue experiments.

claim: These results imply a role for microglia in inducing proliferation in early pre-neoplastic cells.
source: Importantly, these results imply a role for microglia in inducing proliferation in early pre-neoplastic cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the rescue experiments showing that Cxcr4b in macrophages/microglia increases proliferation of AKT1 cells.

claim: The Cxcr4b receptor can be activated by its cognate ligands Sdf1a (Cxcl12a) and Sdf1b (Cxcl12b) and the noncognate ligand macrophage migration inhibitory factor (Mif).
source: The Cxcr4b receptor can be activated by its cognate ligands Sdf1a (Cxcl12a) and Sdf1b (Cxcl12b) and the noncognate ligand macrophage migration inhibitory factor (Mif).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the Cxcr4b receptor.

claim: sdf1a expression levels did not show differences to control cells.
source: While sdf1a expression levels did not show differences to control cells we detected a three-fold increase in mif expression levels and an over 10-fold increase in sdf1b expression levels in AKT1-positive neural cells compared to control cells (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: There was a three-fold increase in mif expression levels in AKT1-positive neural cells compared to control cells.
source: While sdf1a expression levels did not show differences to control cells we detected a three-fold increase in mif expression levels and an over 10-fold increase in sdf1b expression levels in AKT1-positive neural cells compared to control cells (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: There was an over 10-fold increase in sdf1b expression levels in AKT1-positive neural cells compared to control cells.
source: While sdf1a expression levels did not show differences to control cells we detected a three-fold increase in mif expression levels and an over 10-fold increase in sdf1b expression levels in AKT1-positive neural cells compared to control cells (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Sdf1b overexpression in larval brains in the absence of AKT1 overexpression led to significantly increased microglia numbers compared to controls.
source: Injection of a lexOP:sdf1b-lexOP:tagRFP construct into NBT:ΔLexPR transgenic fish led to significantly increased microglia numbers compared to controls (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Higher levels of Sdf1b are sufficient to induce an increase in microglia numbers.
source: Thus, higher levels of Sdf1b are sufficient to induce an increase in microglia numbers.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Sdf1b overexpression experiment.

claim: In the cxcr4b-/- mutant background, Sdf1b overexpression did not impact on microglia numbers.
source: Indeed, in the cxcr4b-/- mutant background, Sdf1b overexpression did not impact on microglia numbers (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: High levels of Sdf1b produced by AKT1 positive cells lead to increased microglia numbers via Cxcr4b activation.
source: Thus, high levels of Sdf1b produced by AKT1 positive cells lead to increased microglia numbers via Cxcr4b activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Sdf1b overexpression and cxcr4b-/- mutant experiments.

claim: Treatment with DEX or Ki20227 had a direct impact on microglia in control and AKT1-positive larvae, leading to significantly reduced microglia numbers.
source: Treatment with DEX or Ki20227 had a direct impact on microglia in control and AKT1-positive larvae, leading to significantly reduced microglia numbers in controls and AKT1 larvae, respectively (Figure 8Ai).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8Ai.

claim: While proliferation rates of neural cells remained constant in controls, DEX and Ki20227-treated AKT1-positive larvae showed a more than 50% reduction in the number of proliferating AKT1 cells compared to DMSO controls.
source: Furthermore, while proliferation rates of neural cells remained constant in controls (Figure 8Aii), DEX and Ki20227-treated AKT1-positive larvae showed a more than 50% reduction in the number of proliferating AKT1 cells compared to DMSO controls (Figure 8Aii).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8Aii.

claim: We did not detect 4C4 positive microglial cells in irf8-/- larvae at 8dpf.
source: In line with published observations, we did not detect 4C4 positive microglial cells in irf8-/- larvae at 8dpf (Figure 8Bi).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8Bi.

claim: Upon AKT1 overexpression in irf8-/- larvae, we detected a small population of 4C4-positive cells.
source: Interestingly, upon AKT1 overexpression in irf8-/- larvae, we detected a small population of 4C4-positive cells (Figure 8Bi).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8Bi.

claim: These cells were probably derived from the population of macrophages that recover in irf8-/- larvae from 7 dpf, which then infiltrated into the brain due to AKT1 overexpression and differentiated into 4C4+ cells.
source: These cells were probably derived from the population of macrophages that recover in irf8-/- larvae from 7 dpf, which then infiltrated into the brain due to AKT1 overexpression and differentiated into 4C4+ cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known recovery of macrophages in irf8-/- larvae.

claim: The number of 4C4-positive cells was 80% lower in irf8-/- larvae compared to wild-type larvae upon AKT1 overexpression.
source: Importantly, the number of 4C4-positive cells was 80% lower in irf8-/- larvae compared to wild-type larvae upon AKT1 overexpression (Figure 8Bi), which allowed us to address the impact on the proliferation of AKT1-positive cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8Bi.

claim: While proliferation rates of neural cells remained constant in irf8-/- controls, we detected an almost 60% reduction in proliferation of AKT1-positive cells compared to AKT1 positive cells in wild-type larvae.
source: While proliferation rates of neural cells remained constant in irf8-/- controls (Figure 8Bii), we detected an almost 60% reduction in proliferation of AKT1-positive cells compared to AKT1 positive cells in wild-type larvae (Figure 8Bii).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 8Bii.

claim: Macrophages and microglia promote proliferation of AKT1-positive cells from the earliest stages of brain tumor growth.
source: In summary, these experiments show that macrophages and microglia promote proliferation of AKT1-positive cells from the earliest stages of brain tumor growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the depletion experiments using DEX, Ki20227, and the irf8-/- mutant.

claim: Infiltrating macrophages are abundant in primary and metastatic brain tumors.
source: Based on multiple models of murine brain malignancy and genetic lineage tracing, Bowman et al. showed that infiltrating macrophages are abundant in primary and metastatic brain tumors (Bowman et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: 85% of the tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) within the glioma were infiltrated monocytes/macrophages.
source: A further study using genetically engineered mouse models to distinguish monocytes/macrophages from microglia showed that 85% of the tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) within the glioma were infiltrated monocytes/macrophages (Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Infiltrating monocytes transitioned to macrophages and microglia-like cells.
source: Furthermore, the authors concluded that infiltrating monocytes transitioned to macrophages and microglia-like cells (Chen et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The increased number of 4C4 positive cells detected in our model might reflect these microglia-like cells.
source: The increased number of 4C4 positive cells detected in our model might reflect these microglia-like cells.
evidence: This is a speculation based on comparison to published data.

claim: This is further supported by our live imaging experiments showing that infiltrating macrophages start expressing p2ry12, which has been shown to be microglia specific across different species.
source: This is further supported by our live imaging experiments showing that infiltrating macrophages start expressing p2ry12, which has been shown to be microglia specific across different species (Crotti and Ransohoff, 2016).
evidence: This is an inference based on the live imaging data and established knowledge about p2ry12.

claim: The CCL2/CCR2 signaling axis seems to be the main attractant for monocytes at the later stages of glioma growth.
source: Interestingly, while the CCL2/CCR2 signaling axis seems to be the main attractant for monocytes at the later stages of glioma growth, we show that Sdf1b/Cxcr4b signaling is responsible for macrophage infiltration during the initial stages of oncogene activation in the brain.
evidence: This is established knowledge stated in the discussion.

claim: Sdf1b/Cxcr4b signaling is responsible for macrophage infiltration during the initial stages of oncogene activation in the brain.
source: Interestingly, while the CCL2/CCR2 signaling axis seems to be the main attractant for monocytes at the later stages of glioma growth, we show that Sdf1b/Cxcr4b signaling is responsible for macrophage infiltration during the initial stages of oncogene activation in the brain.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion based on the data from the study.

claim: A role for SDF1/CXCR4 signaling in macrophage attraction has been described before in rodent models of breast cancer and tumor relapse after chemotherapy.
source: Importantly, a role for SDF1/CXCR4 signaling in macrophage attraction has been described before in rodent models of breast cancer and tumor relapse after chemotherapy (Hughes et al., 2015; Boimel et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Our data show that the pre-neoplastic AKT1 cells produce Sdf1b.
source: Our data show that the pre-neoplastic AKT1 cells produce Sdf1b, which is in line with previous studies showing that AKT1 is involved in activating the expression of SDF1 (Furue et al., 2017; Conley-LaComb et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on qPCR data and comparison to published data.

claim: AKT1 is involved in activating the expression of SDF1.
source: Our data show that the pre-neoplastic AKT1 cells produce Sdf1b, which is in line with previous studies showing that AKT1 is involved in activating the expression of SDF1 (Furue et al., 2017; Conley-LaComb et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Other studies revealed an AKT-mediated induction of the transcription factor specificity protein 1 (Sp1) and Sp1-binding sites were shown to be functional within the human SDF1 promoter.
source: Other studies revealed an AKT-mediated induction of the transcription factor specificity protein 1 (Sp1) and Sp1-binding sites were shown to be functional within the human SDF1 promoter (Gómez-Villafuertes et al., 2015; Pore et al., 2004; García-Moruja et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: AKT1-induced Sdf1b expression might be mediated via Sp1.
source: Thus, AKT1-induced Sdf1b expression might be mediated via Sp1.
evidence: This is a speculation based on established knowledge about AKT1 and Sp1.

claim: Sdf1b produced by the pre-neoplastic cells acts specifically on macrophages and microglia but is not required in an autocrine fashion during these early stages.
source: Furthermore, we show that Sdf1b produced by the pre-neoplastic cells acts specifically on macrophages and microglia but is not required in an autocrine fashion during these early stages.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cell-specific rescue experiments.

claim: Sdf1b/Cxcr4b signaling is not required for proliferation of AKT1-expressing cells in an autocrine fashion during initial stages of oncogenic activation.
source: Thus, Sdf1b/Cxcr4b signaling is not required for proliferation of AKT1-expressing cells in an autocrine fashion during initial stages of oncogenic activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cell-specific rescue experiments.

claim: This might highlight another difference between the early and late stages of tumor growth, as autocrine SDF1/CXCR4 signaling has been shown to be involved in proliferation of various glioma cell lines.
source: This might highlight another difference between the early and late stages of tumor growth, as autocrine SDF1/CXCR4 signaling has been shown to be involved in proliferation of various glioma cell lines (for review see (Gagliardi et al., 2014)).
evidence: This is a speculation based on comparison to established knowledge.

claim: Microglia have been shown to release stress-inducible protein 1 (STI1) for example, which increased proliferation of glioma cells in vitro and in vivo.
source: Microglia have been shown to release stress-inducible protein 1 (STI1) for example, which increased proliferation of glioma cells in vitro and in vivo (Carvalho da Fonseca et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Co-culture studies showed that release of TGF-β by microglia-stimulated glioma growth.
source: Furthermore, co-culture studies showed that release of TGF-β by microglia-stimulated glioma growth (Wesolowska et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The fact that microglia promote the growth of pre-neoplastic cells rather than inhibiting their growth is further supported by the live imaging experiments conducted in this study.
source: Importantly, the fact that microglia promote the growth of pre-neoplastic cells rather than inhibiting their growth is further supported by the live imaging experiments conducted in this study.
evidence: This is an inference based on the live imaging data showing no phagocytosis.

claim: Within the time series acquired to monitor the behavior of macrophages/microglia toward AKT1-positive cells, we did not observe phagocytosis events.
source: As macrophages and microglia are professional phagocytes, they are able to phagocytose cells that are detrimental to the body. However, within the time series acquired to monitor the behavior of macrophages/microglia toward AKT1-positive cells, we did not observe phagocytosis events.
evidence: This is a primary finding based on live imaging data.

claim: Similar observations were made in rodent and zebrafish live imaging models showing direct cellular interactions between microglia and glioma cells.
source: Interestingly, similar observations were made in rodent and zebrafish live imaging models showing direct cellular interactions between microglia and glioma cells (Resende, 2016; Hamilton et al., 2016; Bayerl et al., 2016; Ricard et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Our study highlights that signals stimulating these cellular interactions are produced early upon activation of an oncogene and seem to persist to later stages of tumor growth.
source: Our study highlights that signals stimulating these cellular interactions are produced early upon activation of an oncogene and seem to persist to later stages of tumor growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the live imaging data and comparison to published data.

claim: Microglia have been shown to directly interact with highly active neurons with increased Ca2+ levels.
source: As microglia have been shown to directly interact with highly active neurons with increased Ca2+ levels (Li et al., 2012), it is tempting to speculate that Ca2+ levels might be increased in AKT1-positive cells resulting in ATP/ADP release to promote the observed interactions with microglia.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: It is tempting to speculate that Ca2+ levels might be increased in AKT1-positive cells resulting in ATP/ADP release to promote the observed interactions with microglia.
source: As microglia have been shown to directly interact with highly active neurons with increased Ca2+ levels (Li et al., 2012), it is tempting to speculate that Ca2+ levels might be increased in AKT1-positive cells resulting in ATP/ADP release to promote the observed interactions with microglia.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism underlying the observed interactions.

claim: Macrophage and microglia are activated during the earliest stages of oncogene activation in the brain and develop their pro-tumoural activity immediately by promoting proliferation of pre-neoplastic cells.
source: In summary, we show for the first time that macrophage and microglia are activated during the earliest stages of oncogene activation in the brain and develop their pro-tumoural activity immediately by promoting proliferation of pre-neoplastic cells.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion based on all the data from the study.

claim: It is tempting to speculate that similar interactions occur during tumor recurrence, thus inhibiting the underlying signals might offer additional therapeutic options.
source: It is tempting to speculate that similar interactions occur during tumor recurrence, thus inhibiting the underlying signals might offer additional therapeutic options.
evidence: This is a speculation about the clinical implications of the findings.

claim: Dexamethasone has previously been shown to inhibit macrophages and microglia upon spinal cord injury and brain inflammation in zebrafish.
source: We treated AKT1 overexpressing larvae with the immunosuppressant Dexamethasone (DEX) which has previously been shown to inhibit macrophages and microglia upon spinal cord injury and brain inflammation in zebrafish (Ohnmacht et al., 2016; Kyritsis et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The CSF-1R inhibitor Ki20227 has previously been shown to deplete macrophages and to reduce tumor growth in a rodent melanoma model.
source: Furthermore, to specifically deplete macrophages and microglia, we treated AKT1-expressing larvae with the CSF-1R inhibitor Ki20227 that has previously been shown to deplete macrophages and to reduce tumor growth in a rodent melanoma model (Tham et al., 2015; Ohno et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Interferon regulatory factor 8 (Irf8) is vital for macrophage development in mammals and in teleosts.
source: Interferon regulatory factor 8 (Irf8) is vital for macrophage development in mammals and in teleosts.
evidence: This is established knowledge stated in the results section.

claim: The irf8 null mutant (irf8-/-) zebrafish was characterized to lack macrophages up to around 6 dpf, with recovery from 7 dpf while microglia were absent in the brain until 31 dpf.
source: The irf8 null mutant (irf8-/-) zebrafish was characterized to lack macrophages up to around 6 dpf, with recovery from 7 dpf while microglia were absent in the brain until 31 dpf (Shiau et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.
